items.question: What great attainment makes one dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation together constitute a supreme attainment
Such great accomplishment can arise for a practitioner
This attainment brings favor from the yoginīs
items.inference: One who attains the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes upon emergence in the moon island?
premises: A context of emergence in the moon island is indicated
A chapter is identified by ordinal number
The ninth chapter is thereby marked
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes with the emergence in the moon island.
items.plain_english: Thus the ninth chapter concludes, having emerged in the moon island.

rows.grounds: second member of compound describing self

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is envisioned as surrounded by fire
The posture involves standing on one foot
This forms a specific contemplative image
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self encircled by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request is made to the god regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: A determination concerning knowledge is sought
The god is directly addressed
The request asks for immediate manifestation
items.inference: The speaker asks the god to make the determination of knowledge manifest now.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What division of eight groups of eight is sought to be known fully?
premises: A division consisting of eight groups of eight is mentioned
Complete knowledge of this division is desired
The knowing is described as endless or exhaustive
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and exhaustively the division of the eight groups of eight.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean endlessly or in infinite detail
items.plain_english: I seek to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight groups of eight.

items.question: How does the secret place function as a wheel for swift accomplishment?
premises: A secret place is identified with a wheel
This wheel is associated with accomplishment
The accomplishment occurs quickly
items.inference: The secret place, as a wheel, brings about swift accomplishment.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, how the secret place, as a wheel, is quickly accomplished.

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the goddess for asking a question rare even for gods?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval
The goddess has asked a question
The matter asked about is difficult for gods to obtain
items.inference: Bhairava praises the goddess because she has asked about something rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

items.question: Which bodily locations correspond to the syllables kṣa and laṃ?
premises: The syllable kṣa is assigned a specific locus
The syllable laṃ is assigned another locus
These loci are the brahmarandhra and the forehead
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is the state of the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which bodily locations correspond to the syllables ṣa and śa?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
These assignments are given in sequence
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What follows after the place-wheels have been declared by the teacher?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
A meditation related to them exists
The beloved is instructed to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teacher instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described in form?
premises: A lotus is the object of description
It has eight spokes or petals
It is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: It is a divine eight-spoked lotus, adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: object to be abandoned; sandhi form

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with an even mind adopt through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an even mind
Village customs are presented as something to relinquish
An optative injunction is given
items.inference: Through practice, one with an even mind should abandon village customs.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer to ordinary social or worldly customs
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an even mind, one should abandon the customs of the village.

items.question: What powers arise such as distant hearing and paralysis of bonds?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is mentioned
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned
These are presented as related attainments
items.inference: The attainments include knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: syntactic role of stobham is compressed in this verse
items.plain_english: There is knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the paralysis of bonds, O beloved.

items.question: What further attainments are summarized as immortality and transformation?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment
Transformation is named as another attainment
The list is given in brief
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation.
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief, there are immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized by fiery meditation?
premises: A second lotus is introduced
It has eight petals
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is brightly illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is the eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation
A capacity to make forms is described
These forms can be produced in many ways
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: One whose mind has become one-pointed in meditation can create forms in many ways.

items.question: What destructive power does an angered adept possess over the triple world?
premises: The adept is described as angry
The entire triple world is the object
Both moving and unmoving beings are included
items.inference: When angry, the adept can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function belongs to the third great wheel regarding the nine principles?
premises: A third great wheel is identified
Nine principles are specified
The wheel is described as a liberator
items.inference: The third great wheel functions as the liberator from the nine principles.
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is mentioned
Seeing from very far away is mentioned
These are presented as parallel attainments
items.inference: The practice yields the removal of wrinkles and grey hair and likewise vision from a great distance.
items.plain_english: There is the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise seeing from very far away.

items.question: What practice should be performed in solitude with full intent on meditation?
premises: Solitude is prescribed as the setting
Multiple forms are to be created
The practitioner must be intent on meditation
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create forms in many ways.

items.question: What result comes to one intent on constant practice of this discipline?
premises: Constant practice is maintained
The practitioner is fully intent on it
Immortality is produced as a result
items.inference: One intent on constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death from aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified
Death associated with age is the target
A future overcoming is stated
items.inference: Through abstaining from food by day, one will overcome death from aging.
uncertainties: divasāt nāśanena may mean fasting during the day
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant practice of this yoga over time?
premises: Constant practice through yoga is performed
A duration of sixteen years is indicated
A specific bodily form results
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from always contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored form is contemplated continually
The triple world is the object of effect
A power to shake it is asserted
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: Always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world, O beloved.
